title: USGS Event Summary v3 + Aftershock Forecast v1 — RCC Forward, 12:38

fields.issuer: U.S. Geological Survey, National Earthquake Information Center. Forwarded by the Oregon OEM Regional Coordination Center to eoc@marlowcountyor.example at 12:38 PDT. EXERCISE PRODUCT
fields.mainshock: M 9.0 (REVIEWED, Event Summary version 3; was M 8.9 in version 2), Cascadia Subduction Zone, about 80 km W of Port Alder, Oregon, 2027-04-13 10:14 PDT, depth 20 km. Largest aftershock so far: M 7.5 (REVIEWED, was M 7.6 automatic), about 60 km WNW of Port Alder, 11:52 PDT
fields.issued: Aftershock Forecast issued 2027-04-13 12:30 PDT (version 1), based on Earthquake Event Summary version 3

rows.chance: about 1% (an earthquake larger than the M 9.0 mainshock)

fields.note: These are chances, not predictions. Nobody can say when an aftershock will happen, and nobody can say the aftershocks have ended. Aftershocks become less frequent with time but can still be damaging for weeks to months. Any large aftershock offshore can generate a new local tsunami: strong or long shaking means move to high ground on foot right away, without waiting for a message. A larger earthquake than the mainshock is possible but unlikely. Duty Seismologist, RCC bridge line, 12:38: "Please quote version 3 and the forecast window. Do not round 30 percent to 'unlikely.' This forecast will be updated as the sequence develops; quote the version you used."

instructorNote: Main narrative inject. Watch whether the PIO replaces the outdated 'M 8.9 (v2)' on the 12:20 WebEOC board and writes an aftershock message by 13:00 that gives M 9.0 (version 3), the one-week window and the stated percentages, names the XL and XXL zones and tells people to go uphill again if they feel strong shaking. The TWC should check that message against NTWC Message 4 before release, and the BO should use the 85% chance of an M 6+ aftershock to plan re-inspections and say that a green placard is no guarantee.

citations.quote: Within 30 minutes of a large earthquake the EOC reads, as estimates: the USGS earthquake event summary and magnitude; the ShakeMap shaking intensities; the PAGER loss estimate; and the ground failure

Every message states the NTWC message type, the zone names, the time the message was issued, and one instruction: go to high ground now on foot. Text messages are under 160 characters; WEA is within 3
